description: defk-9vl case supports integer/bool literals, ^pin, _, a variable, and guards with guard-safe ops. Add: `x when x in [1, 2, 3]` with a literal list, and `x when x in 1..10` / `in a..b//s` ranges (lower to comparisons / switch ranges). Compare with Elixir in tests, including CaseClauseError when nothing matches.

comments.text: Decisions: in lowers via Defk.GuardIn, shared by compiler and Elixir mode. Lists: literal ints or bools (=== chain), [] is false. Ranges: literal bounds/step computed at compile time (last reached element, bounds, rem(x,k) in {r, r-k}), exact Enum.member? semantics incl. negative steps and empty ranges; no runtime overflow. Variable bounds allowed only with explicit //1 or //-1 (Elixir rejects bare a..b in guards; other steps need literals). Step nonzero and within +-(2^63-1). LHS must be i64 (bool for bool lists): float lhs rejected since 1.0 in 1..3 is false in Elixir. All errors reuse case-guard (summary updated, docs section synced).

title: More case patterns: literal-list in guards and ranges
